title: Use a single shared spend dashboard
context: Three fictional teams at Northlight Studios track AI spend in three separate spreadsheets, and nobody can answer what the studio spends in a month.
decision: Adopt one shared dashboard, updated monthly from exported usage files, owned by the program manager.
alternatives: Keep per-team sheets; buy a vendor spend-management tool.

title: Every agent gets a registry entry before it ships
context: Agents at Harbor Lane Studio (fictional) were being deployed with no owner and no record of what data they could touch, so a cost spike took a week to trace.
decision: No agent ships without a registry entry: owner, scope, data access, model/tool, and status. Revocation goes through the registry.
alternatives: Keep a wiki page updated by hand; require approval in chat only.

title: Demo data is fictional and labeled as such
context: Example data in public repos kept looking like real customer data, which confused reviewers and risked leaking real figures.
decision: All sample data in public repos uses fictional names (e.g. Northlight Studios) and is labeled fictional in the README and in the data itself.
alternatives: Use anonymized real data; use obviously fake names without labels.

title: Kill-switch decisions are recorded, not just acted on
context: A tool was paused in a chat thread and nobody could later say who paused it, when, or why — so it was quietly re-enabled.
decision: Every pause/kill decision is recorded in the tool's kill-switch list with owner, reason, and timestamp, and the record outlives the action.
alternatives: Record pauses in chat only; rely on vendor audit logs.
